summary: John's maternal great-grandmother, wife of James Petriello; daughter of Bisaccia immigrants Frank Giannetta and the foundling Angelica Ferrantino.
bio:
The Ancestry tree showed only 'Mollie Petriello 1911-' as James's wife; Round 1 initially wondered if Mollie = Mary Cognetti and then corrected that (Mollie b. 1911 is James's wife and John T.'s mother; maiden name unknown). Round 2 solved her identity: Carmela 'Mollie' Gianetta, b. 13 Jul 1910 Dunmore, d. 7 Feb 2000 Scranton (FS tree GQ4M-KCR, 6 sources incl. 1950 census 'Mollie Petriello' and SSDI 'Mollie C Petriello', the C = Carmela). The tree's 1911 should be 1910. On the 1931 marriage license (No. 1107, sworn 20 Jun 1931) she is 'Mollie Genett', 20, housework, born Dunmore, living at 133 Sand St; father Frank, a blacksmith born in Italy, living in Dunmore; mother Angeli(c)a, maiden name Ferrandino, born in Italy. Her mother 'Angelina Genett' consented because she was a minor. Married at Dunmore in July 1931 (FS: 12 Jul 1931) by Rev. Michael DeLarno. 133 Sand St was also her father's address on his 1920 Declaration of Intention. Her siblings were Savino (1897-1964), Mariano Martin (1899-1941), Maria (1902), Antonio (1907-1998), Giuseppe (1912-1971), Rosa (1914) and Charles J. (1916-1975).

In January 1920 'Molly', aged 9, was living with her parents Frank and Angelina 'Genet' at 133 Sand Street in Dunmore's 5th Ward, the only daughter then at home among five brothers ([R4-S3]). Her parents had married about 1896 in Bisaccia, and her four older siblings were born in Italy. She was the first of the children born in Dunmore, in July 1910, three months after the April 1910 census listed the family at no. 134 ([R4-S4]). After her 1931 marriage she lived with James at 1028 Bunker Hill Street in Scranton, where the 1940 census records her schooling as 5th grade ([R4-S1]). By 1950 they were back on Sand Street at no. 128, a few doors from her widowed mother at no. 133 and next door to her sister Mary Pichiarello. Mollie was then working part-time as a sewing-machine operator in a lingerie factory, one of the garment shops that employed many Dunmore Italian women ([R4-S2]).
